title: Hybrid IO pricing experiment: asymmetric input/output rates with partial streaming proxy
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Summary: Run a controlled experiment to evaluate an asymmetric input/output per-token rate structure combined with a partial-streaming proxy (hybrid mode) and a streaming minimum. Goal is to improve unit economics for high-output batch workloads while preserving predictable revenue for streaming-heavy integrations and minimizing churn for enterprise customers with contracts. This ticket captures experiment design, engineering requirements, sales/legal guardrails for contracts and questionnaires, rollout plan, and success criteria.

Context: Many customers use a mix of short request/long-response (e.g., code generation, summarization) and conversational streaming. Current symmetric IO pricing conflates cost signals: servers bear higher GPU work for output tokens but customers are sensitive to input volume for embedding-like workloads. Streaming introduces operational differences (long-lived connections, proxies) that we can charge or discount differently. Prior experiments looked at symmetric floors and tiered streaming minimums; this experiment explores asymmetric unit rates (input < output) plus a small per-minute streaming connection surcharge and an adjustable streaming minimum to protect revenue for low-volume but long-lived streams.

Hypothesis: An asymmetric IO price that charges ~0.6x for inputs vs outputs plus a modest streaming connection fee and a 5000-token monthly streaming minimum will: 1) reduce overcharging for input-heavy workloads, lowering churn for developer-first customers; 2) increase revenue capture for output-heavy workloads without raising sticker prices for lightweight conversational customers; 3) maintain or improve gross margin by aligning billing with GPU/throughput cost.

Key trade-offs: Simplicity vs precision (more complex billing may increase support load and Qs from customers). Risk of customer confusion requiring updated docs, SDK changes, and sales playbooks. Legal & enterprise security questionnaires may require explicit clarifications about streaming connection fees and minimums in contracts. Engineering must implement meter delta tracking, tagging by delivery mode (stream vs non-stream), and a proxy-enabled metric to ensure accurate attribution.

Experiment variants:
- Variant A (control): current symmetric IO pricing with existing streaming minimums.
- Variant B (asymmetric IO only): input token rate = 0.6 * output token rate; no streaming connection fee; streaming minimum = 0.
- Variant C (hybrid): asymmetric IO + streaming connection fee ($0.01 per concurrent-minute) + monthly streaming minimum (5,000 streaming-output tokens) with credits applied for Reserved Capacity customers.
- Variant D (enterprise-only probe): offer hybrid pricing to enterprise direct-sold customers during renewal as an optional add-on with clear FAQ and contract language.

Experiment duration and cohorts: 8 weeks with 3 customer cohorts: self-serve free/credit accounts (low-touch), PLG growth customers (mid-touch), and enterprise (sales-handled). Randomize PLG accounts into control/B/C but enterprise gets D as opt-in only. Monitor early telemetry during week 2 for unintended billing spikes.

Engineering work: Metering: add per-request flags: delivery_mode (streaming|non-streaming), streaming_connection_minutes, streaming_prefix_tokens (for partial streaming where prefix is buffered server-side). Billing: support asymmetric per-token rates and apply streaming connection surcharge in billing pipeline and invoices. SDK: client-side header for intended delivery_mode to help attribution (fallback to server detection). Console: add per-route breakdown by input/output tokens and streaming minutes.

Sales/legal action items: Draft contract FAQ language for streaming minimums and connection fee; update SOW templates; prepare one-pager for AE playbook explaining when to recommend hybrid pricing and how it affects committed commitments. Prepare responses for common security questionnaire items: data flow for streaming proxy, logs/retention, and encryption-in-transit for long-lived connections.

Telemetry & dashboards: create dashboard showing delta ARR, churn, ARPA, avg cost-per-output-token (GPU-weighted), fraction of requests flagged streaming, and billing complaints/CS tickets. Build a daily job to compute realized margin impact by cohort.

Accept criteria and success metrics: see success_metrics below.
acceptance_criteria: Billing pipeline emits correct asymmetric IO charges for test accounts (verified against golden metered logs)
Console shows per-route input/output split and streaming minutes within 48 hours of experiment start
No >5% spike in support tickets related to billing confusion during first 2 weeks
Experiment model projects >= 3% net ARR uplift for PLG cohort or >= 15% ARR uplift when offered to enterprise opt-ins without increasing churn >1%
Legal approved contract language and AE playbook published before enterprise opt-in (release gating)
success_metrics: Net ARR delta attributable to experiment (cohort-adjusted)
Change in average realized gross margin per-token (GPU-weighted)
Number of billing support tickets per 1k customers
Adoption rate of hybrid pricing in enterprise opt-ins
runbook: Week 0: finalize rates and fees; legal and finance sign-off; engineering triage
Week 1: deploy metering + console telemetry to canary namespace; smoke test with internal accounts
Week 2: ramp to 10% PLG cohort; monitor billing, support, and latency impact; rollback guard if billing delta > 10x expected or support > threshold
Week 3-6: run full cohort experiment; daily monitoring and weekly cross-functional sync
Week 7: analyze results, prepare deck for exec review; draft recommended pricing rollout
Week 8: decide (rollout / iterate / cancel) and communicate to customers
risks: Increased billing complexity leading to higher support volume and degraded developer experience
Misattribution of streaming vs non-streaming requests causing incorrect charges
Enterprise customers push back during renewal, requiring credits or concessions
Edge cases: partial-server-side buffering (prefixes) that look like input tokens but are billed differently leading to disputes
mitigations: Clear docs + SDK header to indicate intended delivery_mode and opt-in detection fallback
Grace period credits for first invoice for test cohorts to reduce dispute risk
Detailed reconciliation tooling and easy refund flow in billing portal
Sales playbook with concrete migration slides and ARR modeling for customers

notes: Avoid language 'streaming surcharge' in public docs; prefer 'streaming connection fee' and show example invoices
Consider tiered connection fee for high-concurrency enterprise customers to avoid penalizing websocket-heavy integration patterns
If experiment shows >5% self-serve churn, halt rollout and re-evaluate minimum thresholds
